requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted read-write at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: The executor created /dev/vg_srv/lv_data, formatted it as XFS, and mounted it read-write at /srv/data. Final post-restart evidence shows the 2.00 GiB LV active and still mounted there.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted and preserve its contents.
requirements.summary: Before growth, the LV was 1.00 GiB with mount ID 379 and two recorded file hashes. It was extended to 2.00 GiB and XFS grew to 2,080,374,784 bytes; mount ID 379 remained unchanged throughout, and both hashes matched afterward. Post-restart evidence confirms the size, mount, and contents remained intact.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transition evidence. The LV was mounted, expanded online from 1.00 to 2.00 GiB without changing the mount identity, and its contents retained matching hashes. The mandatory node restart also demonstrated successful persistence and recovery.
limitations: Lifecycle snapshots are generic and do not independently inventory the new mount, LVM configuration, or installed package list; those facts are established by the detailed executor evidence.

The hygiene assessment treats the unused /run marker as temporary residue cleared by reboot; no explicit deletion observation was captured, though /run is volatile and post-restart evidence used a different boot.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was focused and left the node healthy: package consistency remained good, no failed services appeared, and listening exposure did not change. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged scheduled reboot, connection disruption, a different boot ID, and recovered system, service, LVM, mount, filesystem, and data state. The only identifiable unnecessary mutation was writing /run/srv-data-loopdev in cmd-6d82800c605142cd; subsequent commands rediscovered the loop device instead of using this file. It was low-risk and was automatically removed by the reboot. All other mutations had clear roles in creating, growing, persisting, verifying, or restarting the requested storage.
